html:
The Kokoda Track campaign was fought in 1942 along a mountain path across the Owen Stanley Range, as Japanese troops tried to reach Port Moresby overland. Australian soldiers stopped them close to the town and pushed them back.

The fighting was in rain, mud and jungle, and disease killed and sickened as many as bullets. Papuan carriers bore supplies and carried the wounded out; Australians called them the Fuzzy Wuzzy Angels.

Kokoda, with the Guadalcanal campaign, marked the end of Japan's advance in the South Pacific in the Pacific War. In Australia it is remembered beside Gallipoli as a defining war story. The war left New Guinea's coasts wrecked.
